review.notes: Built on the course: import stages and roles, lead time sum, pre-arrival work, Incoterms groups, risk vs cost, sea-only rules for containers, CIF vs CIP insurance, EXW/DDP traps, payment risk ladder, D/P vs D/A, UCP 600, discrepancies, B/L types. Calculations checked. Fictional companies.

content.company: Granite Machinery Parts (fictional), importing machine parts and tools by container
content.briefing: You manage imports end to end: contracts, Incoterms, payment terms, documents and clearance. A new supplier from Asia is starting, and the finance director wants fewer delays and safer payments.

variants.text: Production 21 days, to port 4 days, sea transit 35 days, clearance 10 days, delivery 2 days. What is the import lead time?

choices.f: Correct: add every stage. You plan the order 72 days before stock is needed.
That is only sea transit. Every stage adds time.
You left out clearance and delivery.

variants.text: The vessel has just sailed. Arrival is in 30 days. What do you do now?

choices.t: Get document copies, check them, send to the broker
choices.f: Errors found now are fixed before arrival. Clearance takes 3 days, not 10.

choices.t: Wait for the ship to arrive, then start
choices.f: Document problems found at arrival cause storage charges.

choices.t: Ask the supplier to call when it arrives
choices.f: The supplier's job is done. Pre-arrival work is yours.

variants.text: The supplier offers EXW factory. Export clearance in their country is hard for a foreign buyer. What is the risk?

choices.t: You must clear export in their country
choices.f: The EXW trap. FCA puts export clearance on the seller.

choices.t: No risk: EXW is the simplest rule
choices.f: Simple for the seller. The buyer does everything.

choices.t: The seller pays the main freight
choices.f: Under EXW, the buyer pays everything from the factory.

variants.text: A supplier proposes DDP Luanda. What is the trap for the supplier?

choices.t: They must clear import and pay duties here
choices.f: Few foreign sellers can do that well. Delays at customs follow.

choices.t: They carry no risk until loading
choices.f: DDP is the maximum seller obligation.

choices.t: The buyer must arrange sea freight
choices.f: Under DDP the seller arranges transport.

variants.text: Goods go in a container, handed over at the inland terminal. Is FOB correct?

choices.f: FOB is for sea goods loaded on board. Containers are handed over at the terminal.

choices.t: Yes: FOB covers all sea cargo
choices.f: Risk stays with the seller after handover, an unclear gap.

choices.t: Yes, if the price is lower
choices.f: Price does not fix the risk mismatch.

variants.text: Under CPT Luanda, the seller pays freight to Luanda. When does risk pass to you?

choices.t: At handover to the first carrier
choices.f: C rules: cost runs to destination, risk passes at origin.
That confuses cost and risk.
Clearance does not move risk.

variants.text: You buy high-value parts CIF. What insurance does CIF require of the seller?

choices.f: Correct. For wider cover, ask for CIP (Clauses A) or insure yourself.
That is CIP's level under Incoterms 2020.
CIF includes insurance, but only minimum.

variants.text: How do you write the rule in the contract?

choices.f: Rule, exact named place and version.

choices.t: FCA China, under the latest Incoterms
choices.f: A country is too vague. Where exactly does risk pass?
No exact place and no version.

variants.text: First order with a new supplier: USD 180,000. Trust is low on both sides. Which method?

choices.f: Banks commit to pay against complying documents. Both sides are protected.
Best for the seller, riskiest for you.
Best for the buyer; the new supplier will refuse.

variants.text: After 2 years of good orders with this supplier, the bank costs of LCs feel high.

choices.t: Move to collection or open account
choices.f: As trust grows, move down the ladder and cut bank costs.

choices.t: Keep using LCs forever to be safe
choices.f: Safe, but expensive once trust is proven.
That raises your risk for no reason.

variants.text: Under a documentary collection 'D/P', when do you get the documents?

choices.f: Documents against payment. D/A means against acceptance of a bill.
That is D/A.
The bank holds documents until payment.

variants.text: Under UCP 600, how long do banks have to examine documents?

choices.f: Correct. Plan cash and release around it.
That is the usual presentation limit after shipment.
Examination is separate from arrival.

variants.text: The LC requires shipment by 30 June. The bill of lading shows 2 July.

choices.t: A discrepancy: the bank may refuse
choices.f: Late shipment does not comply. Seek an amendment or a waiver.
Banks deal in documents, not intentions. Any mismatch counts.

choices.t: The bank will fix the date
choices.f: Banks examine; they do not correct documents.

variants.text: The LC says '500 drill bits'; the invoice says '500 cutting tools'. What do you do?

choices.t: Ask the supplier to match the LC wording
choices.f: Descriptions must match the credit. Fixed before presentation.

choices.t: Present it; it is the same item
choices.f: A wording mismatch is a classic discrepancy.

choices.t: Ask the bank to accept it as is
choices.f: Possible as a waiver, but fixing it first is safer.

variants.text: The forwarder issues you a B/L; the shipping line issues one to the forwarder. Which is yours?

choices.f: The forwarder's house B/L. The master B/L is between line and forwarder.
That one is issued by the shipping line to the forwarder.
Each has a different issuer and holder.

variants.text: You want a bill of lading that can be transferred to your bank by endorsement.

choices.f: Transferable by endorsement, often required under LCs.
Named consignee, not transferable.
Not a document of title.

variants.text: The commercial invoice is missing the HS code. Why does it matter?

choices.t: Customs uses it to classify and set duty
choices.f: Without it, clearance stalls and duty may be wrong.

choices.t: It does not matter for customs
choices.f: The HS code drives classification and duty.
Customs relies on it first.

variants.text: Documents arrive with different weights on the invoice, packing list and B/L.

choices.t: Fix them so all documents match
choices.f: Consistency avoids customs queries and LC refusals.
Choosing does not fix inconsistent documents.
Mismatches trigger inspections and delays.

variants.text: Who books the ship and coordinates transport, documents and customs agents?

choices.f: The forwarder coordinates; the broker handles clearance.
Depends on the Incoterm, and the forwarder does the work.
Customs controls, it does not coordinate.

variants.text: What belongs in the import file?

choices.f: One complete file speeds clearance and audits.
Customs and audits need much more.
The B/L alone cannot clear goods.
